summary: Which bracha we make before eating fruit, wine, bread, and vegetables.
stIntro: This mishna discusses the blessings recited over various foods.

chunks.en: How do we make a bracha on fruits?
chunks.st: How does one recite a blessing over fruits?

chunks.en: On fruit from a tree, one says,
chunks.st: Over different fruits that grow on a tree one recites:

chunks.en: "Borei pri ha'etz" (Who creates fruit of the tree),
chunks.st: Who creates fruit of the tree,

chunks.en: except for wine,
chunks.st: with the exception of wine.
chunks.stMore: Although wine is produced from fruit of the tree, due to its significance, its blessing differs from other fruits of the tree.

chunks.he: שֶׁעַל הַיַּיִן אוֹמֵר בּוֹרֵא פְּרִי הַגָּפֶן.
chunks.en: because on wine one says "Borei pri hagafen" (Who creates fruit of the vine).
chunks.st: Over wine one recites: Who creates fruit of the vine.

chunks.en: And on fruits that grow from the ground, one says
chunks.st: Over fruits that grow from the earth, one recites:

chunks.en: "Borei pri ha'adamah" (Who creates fruit of the ground),
chunks.st: Who creates fruit of the ground,

chunks.en: except for bread,
chunks.st: with the exception of bread.
chunks.stMore: Bread, too, is significant and its blessing differs from other fruits of the ground,

chunks.en: because on bread one says
chunks.st: as over bread one recites:

chunks.en: "Hamotzi lechem min ha'aretz" (Who brings bread out of the earth).
chunks.st: Who brings forth bread from the earth.

chunks.he: וְעַל הַיְרָקוֹת אוֹמֵר בּוֹרֵא פְּרִי הָאֲדָמָה.
chunks.en: And on vegetables one says "Borei pri ha'adamah."
chunks.st: Over herbs and leafy vegetables one recites: Who creates fruit of the ground.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says
chunks.stMore: that there is room to distinguish between fruits that grow from the earth, herbs, and leafy vegetables. Although they are all fruit of the ground, since they have different qualities, the blessing on the latter is:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: "Who creates many kinds of herbs."
chunks.st: Who creates various kinds of herbs.

summary: If you made the wrong bracha on food, sometimes it still counts, and "Shehakol" works for everything.
stIntro: This mishna discusses how, after the fact, a more general blessing exempts one from the obligation to recite a more specific one.

chunks.he: בֵּרַךְ עַל פֵּרוֹת הָאִילָן בּוֹרֵא פְּרִי הָאֲדָמָה,
chunks.en: If someone said "Borei pri ha'adamah" on fruit from a tree,
chunks.st: One who recited: Who creates fruit of the ground, over fruit of the tree,

chunks.en: he has done the mitzvah.
chunks.st: fulfilled his obligation.

words.note: He did the mitzvah and does not need to say it again.

chunks.he: וְעַל פֵּרוֹת הָאָרֶץ בּוֹרֵא פְּרִי הָעֵץ,
chunks.en: But if he said "Borei pri ha'etz" on fruits from the ground,
chunks.st: One who recited: Who creates fruit of the tree, over fruits of the earth,

chunks.en: he has not done the mitzvah.
chunks.st: did not fulfill his obligation.

chunks.he: עַל כֻּלָּם אִם אָמַר שֶׁהַכֹּל נִהְיָה, יָצָא:
chunks.en: On all foods, if he said "Shehakol," he has done the mitzvah.
chunks.st: And over all food items, one who recited: By whose word all things came to be, fulfilled his obligation.

words.note: The bracha "Shehakol," meaning everything came to be by Hashem's word.

summary: Foods that don't grow from the ground get the bracha "Shehakol."

chunks.he: עַל דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין גִּדּוּלוֹ מִן הָאָרֶץ
chunks.en: On something that does not grow from the ground
chunks.st: And over a food item whose growth is not from the ground,

chunks.en: one says "Shehakol."
chunks.st: one recites: By whose word all things came to be.

chunks.en: On vinegar, and on spoiled dates,
chunks.st: And over vinegar, wine that fermented and spoiled, and over novelot, dates that spoiled,
chunks.basisNote: Bartenura: novelos are fruits that fell from the tree before they were ripe.

words.note: Wine that went sour.
Dates that went bad.

chunks.en: and on locusts, one says "Shehakol."
chunks.st: and over locusts, one recites: By whose word all things came to be.

words.note: A kind of grasshopper; some kinds are kosher.

chunks.en: On milk and on cheese
chunks.st: So too, over milk, and over cheese,

chunks.en: and on eggs, one says "Shehakol."
chunks.st: and over eggs, one recites: By whose word all things came to be.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: anything that comes from a curse, like spoiled food,
chunks.st: Over any food item that is a type resulting from a curse,

chunks.en: we do not make a bracha on it.
chunks.st: one does not recite a blessing over it at all.
chunks.stMore: None of the items listed exist under normal conditions, and they come about as the result of a curse.

summary: If you have many foods in front of you, which one do you make the bracha on first?

chunks.en: If there were many kinds of food in front of him,
chunks.st: On a different note: If there were many types of food before him,
chunks.stMore: over which food should he recite a blessing first?

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: if one of them is from the seven special foods of Eretz Yisrael,
chunks.st: If there is one of the seven species for which Eretz Yisrael was praised among them,

words.note: The seven special foods of Eretz Yisrael, like grapes, figs, and dates.

chunks.en: he makes the bracha on that one first.
chunks.st: he recites the first blessing over it.

chunks.en: And the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: he makes the bracha on whichever one he wants.
chunks.st: He recites a blessing over whichever of them he wants.

summary: When one bracha covers other foods too, so you don't need a new bracha.
stIntro: This mishna explains those cases and those circumstances in which blessings recited over particular foods exempt other foods at the meal from the requirement to recite a blessing over them.

chunks.en: If he made a bracha on the wine before the meal,
chunks.st: One who recited a blessing over the wine that one drank before the meal,

chunks.en: it also covers the wine after the meal.
chunks.st: with that blessing he exempted the wine that he drinks after the meal.
chunks.basisNote: Bartenura says this is on Shabbos and Yom Tov, when wine is planned for after the meal.

words.note: He doesn't need another bracha for it.

chunks.en: If he made a bracha on the appetizers before the meal,
chunks.st: Similarly, one who recited a blessing over the appetizers that one ate before the meal,

words.note: Small foods eaten before or after a meal, like appetizers.

chunks.en: it also covers the appetizers after the meal.
chunks.st: with that blessing he exempted the appetizers that he eats after the meal.

chunks.en: If he made a bracha on the bread,
chunks.st: One who recited a blessing over the bread

chunks.en: it covers the appetizers,
chunks.st: exempted the appetizers, as they are considered secondary to the bread.

chunks.en: but a bracha on the appetizers
chunks.st: However, one who recited a blessing over the appetizers

chunks.en: does not cover the bread.
chunks.st: did not exempt the bread.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

words.note: Beis Shammai are the students of Shammai, a great early Rabbi.

chunks.en: it does not even cover a cooked dish.
chunks.st: The blessing recited over the appetizers did not exempt even a cooked dish that he eats during the meal.

words.note: Food cooked in a pot.

summary: When people eat together, sometimes one person makes the bracha for everyone.

chunks.en: If people were sitting to eat, not as one group,
chunks.st: If several people were sitting to eat not in the framework of a joint meal,

chunks.en: each one makes his own bracha.
chunks.st: each recites a blessing for himself.

chunks.en: If they reclined together for a meal, one makes the bracha for all of them.
chunks.st: If they were reclined on divans to eat, which renders it a joint meal, one recites a blessing on behalf of them all.

words.note: Long ago, people ate a real meal together leaning on couches.

chunks.en: If wine was brought to them during the meal,
chunks.st: Additionally: If wine came before them during the meal,

chunks.en: each one makes his own bracha on it.
chunks.st: each and every diner recites a blessing over the wine for himself.

chunks.en: If it came after the meal,
chunks.st: If the wine came after the meal,

chunks.en: one makes the bracha for all of them.
chunks.st: one recites a blessing on behalf of them all.

chunks.en: And that same person says the bracha on the sweet-smelling incense,
chunks.st: And he, who recited the blessing over the wine, also says the blessing over the incense [mugmar],
chunks.basisNote: Steinsaltz: the one who blessed the wine. Bartenura: the one who led bentching.

words.note: Sweet-smelling spices burned on coals after a meal.

chunks.en: even though they only bring
chunks.st: although they only bring

chunks.en: the incense after the meal.
chunks.st: the incense to the diners after the meal.

summary: When one food is the main food and another is just a side, we make the bracha on the main food.

chunks.he: הֵבִיאוּ לְפָנָיו מָלִיחַ בַּתְּחִלָּה וּפַת עִמּוֹ,
chunks.en: If they brought him salty food first, with bread alongside it,
chunks.st: If they brought salted food before him to eat first and bread with it,

words.note: Salty food eaten after sweet fruit; bread helps him eat it.

chunks.he: מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַמָּלִיחַ וּפוֹטֵר אֶת הַפַּת,
chunks.en: he makes the bracha on the salty food, and that covers the bread,
chunks.st: he recites a blessing over the salted food and thereby exempts the bread,

chunks.en: because the bread is just a side to it.
chunks.explain: He only eats the bread to help him eat the salty food.
chunks.st: because the salted food is primary while the bread is secondary to it.

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: This is the principle:

chunks.en: whenever there is a main food with a side food,
chunks.st: Any food that is primary and a secondary food is with it,

chunks.he: מְבָרֵךְ עַל הָעִקָּר וּפוֹטֵר אֶת הַטְּפֵלָה:
chunks.en: you make the bracha on the main food, and that covers the side food.
chunks.st: one recites a blessing over the primary and, in so doing, exempts the secondary from its own blessing.

summary: Which bracha to say after eating special fruits, vegetables, or drinking water.

chunks.en: If someone ate figs, grapes, and pomegranates,
chunks.st: One who ate from the fruit for which Eretz Yisrael was praised, grapes and figs and pomegranates,

chunks.en: he says after them the three brachos of bentching, like after bread,
chunks.st: recites the three blessings of Grace after Meals, as he would after eating bread;

words.note: The three main brachos of bentching after a bread meal.

chunks.en: so says Rabban Gamliel.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabban Gamliel.

words.note: "Rabban" is a title for the head of the Sages.
A great Rabbi of the Mishnah, the leader of the Sages.

chunks.en: And the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: only one bracha that is a short form of the three.
chunks.st: One need only recite one blessing abridged from the three blessings of Grace after Meals.

words.note: This is the short after-bracha, like Al Ha'etz.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:
chunks.stMore: The three blessings of Grace after Meals are not restricted to bread; rather,

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: even if he ate cooked vegetables and that is his main food,
chunks.st: even if one ate boiled vegetables, but it is his primary sustenance,

chunks.en: he says after it the three brachos of bentching.
chunks.st: he recites the three blessings of Grace after Meals.

chunks.en: Someone who drinks water because he is thirsty
chunks.st: Additionally: One who drinks water to quench his thirst

chunks.en: says "Shehakol nihyeh bidvaro" (everything came to be by His word).
chunks.st: recites: By whose word all things came to be.

chunks.en: Rabbi Tarfon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Tarfon says:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: "Borei nefashos rabos" (Who creates many living things and their needs).
chunks.st: He recites: Who creates the many forms of life and their needs.
